content: Nanomaterials are engineered on an extremely small scale, which imparts unique and novel properties to the material. This innovation leads to the development of superior consumer and commercial products, as well as advancements in medical treatments. A nanoparticle is extraordinarily small, approximately 1,000,000 times smaller than an ant. However, nanoparticles can exhibit specific toxicological properties. These include the potential to form respirable fibers, which can be inhaled and pose risks to respiratory health. Additionally, granular biopersistent particles, which are particles that resist breakdown within biological systems, may also present health concerns. Nanomaterials can be categorized into various groups based on their composition, structure, and properties. In essence, a nanoparticle is defined as a particle that exists on the nanoscale, typically ranging in size from 1 to 100 nanometers.
